findings.change: Compact living particles into GPU instance buffers in original slot order. Skip dead-slot matrix/color/alpha work, upload only the living prefix and draw only living instances. Use dynamic buffer usage.
findings.visualResult: Six deterministic WebGL scenes have identical SHA-256 framebuffer hashes before and after; emission, physics, materials and quality budgets are unchanged.

findings.change: Precompute the deterministic node hash offsets once per controller instead of hashing node strings for each phase query. Existing signal timings and phase rules are preserved.

findings.evidence: Physics occupies approximately 67-74% of measured CPU frame time; world.step is the largest named individual stage in these runs.
findings.candidate: Profile wheel support raycasts and temporary footprint/actor data under 102 and 300 cars; preserve fixed timestep, collision rules, solver quality and public snapshot isolation.

findings.evidence: Existing instancing, model LOD, object pools, faded-building cache and resource disposal are already present.
findings.candidate: Measure postprocessing, caster coverage and batch culling separately before changing them; current changes retain shadow size, DPR, blur, lighting and draw distance.
RepairPickupVisuals transforms, miniature blur renderer-state vectors, and main actor snapshots can reuse internal scratch data. They are secondary to the measured physics cost.

build.note: Existing large Three.js chunk warning remains.

conclusion: Particle CPU packing is 2.1-17.8 times faster in isolated frozen-time tests and dead instances are removed from GPU submission. Whole-game frame CPU p95 overlaps between repeats, so no robust overall FPS percentage is claimed. Frame interval p95 stays approximately 16.8 ms.
